## $x_1$-wall corner refresh inside tangential ghost slabs {#sec-ch03-cornerrefresh}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: src/mesh/meshblock.cpp, src/bc/bc_func.hpp, src/mesh/mesh.cpp, tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp

-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: after the tangential exchange, each installed $x_1$ boundary function except outflow is applied again
inside the $x_2$ and $x_3$ ghost slabs, so the ghost corners next to an $x_1$ wall match the updated column.
**Switch**: none. **Default**: always on in the block's per-stage sync. **Requires**: boundary functions that give the
same ghosts when called again on an $n_g$-wide slab. **Order**: exact. **Defining rule**: stated in the Derivation
layer.
:::

The tangential exchange fills the $x_2$ and $x_3$ ghost slabs with the neighbour's interior, but within those slabs the
$x_1$ ghost rows (the corners next to an $x_1$ wall) hold whatever the neighbour's wall wrote last, or stale values on
a periodic edge. A stencil with cross-derivatives, such as viscosity next to the wall, then reads a wall corner that
does not belong to this column. Re-applying the $x_1$ boundary function on the slabs makes those corners the wall
ghosts of the updated slab. In the history: [chengcli/snapy#265](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/265).

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; it is a consistency rule. For each installed $x_1$ bfunc that is not outflow, and each
tangential direction with more than one cell, the bfunc is called on the first and last $g = \min(n_g, n/2)$ cells of
that direction, unless that tangential face is itself physical and not periodic, in which case its own bfunc already
wrote the corner. The rule relies on the contract stated with the `BC_FUNCTION` macro: a face function called again on
a tangential slab must not depend on the slab's size and must give the same ghosts ([`bc_func.hpp:28-35`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.hpp#L28-L35)).
Outflow is excluded because its background must match the whole block and it needs primitives.

### Numerical method

The refresh runs at the end of every per-stage sync, on `hydro_u` as conserved and on `scalar_s` as scalar, after
both exchanges and before the scalar primitive is rebuilt. It writes only $x_1$ ghost rows inside the tangential ghost
slabs. @fig-ch03-cornerrefresh-wall shows the cells it rewrites.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-cornerrefresh-wall
#| fig-cap: "An $x_1$ wall (thick line) meeting an $x_2$ block seam (dashed purple). The tangential ghost slab (hatched) is filled by the exchange; its cells below the wall (green) are then rewritten by the $x_1$ wall function, so they mirror this side of the seam rather than holding the neighbour's earlier values."
#| fig-alt: "A grid corner where a horizontal wall meets a vertical seam; the ghost cells below the wall on the far side of the seam are highlighted."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_cornerrefresh_wall import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| refresh after the exchange | [`meshblock.cpp:932-974`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L932-L974) | `refresh` | none |
| contract of a boundary function | [`bc_func.hpp:28-35`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.hpp#L28-L35) | `BC_FUNCTION` | none |

: Code map of the corner refresh. {#tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-code):

1. `physical` is true for an installed, non-periodic tangential face ([`meshblock.cpp:945-950`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L945-L950)).
2. `refresh` loops over the two $x_1$ faces, skips a missing or `is_outflow` function and an $x_1$ axis of one cell,
   and calls the function on each tangential slab whose face is not `physical` ([`meshblock.cpp:951-971`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L951-L971)).
3. It runs for `hydro_u` and `scalar_s` with their types ([`meshblock.cpp:972-973`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L972-L973) for `refresh`).

skips without a GPU. One process. Their pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones` does not refresh corners; only the block's per-stage sync does.
- Only $x_1$ walls are refreshed; $x_2$-$x_3$ corners are synthesised (@sec-ch03-exchange).
:::

The `Mesh`-level sync is a plain exchange ([`mesh.cpp:389-396`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L389-L396) for `exchange_ghost_zones`). A user boundary
function that breaks the contract would write wrong corners without an error (read from the code; not measured). The
switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
